<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par131 />{{GHGmargin-letter|131|f}}
(''e'') Collocation of the ''thing'' and its ''name'', e.g. {{GHGheb|text=בְּהַֽרֲרָם שֵׁעִיר|translate=in their mountainous district, Seir}} (perhaps only a later gloss), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=14|verse=6}}; {{GHGheb|text=הָאָ֫רֶץ כְּנָ֑עַן|translate=the land Canaan}} ({{GHGheb|text=כנען}} probably only a later gloss), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=34|verse=2}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ezr|chapter=9|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=5|verse=9}} (see under ''g'' below).—For examples of nouns in the construct state before a noun in apposition, see {{GHGpar|130|e}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|131|g}}
Rem. 1. Only in certain combinations does the noun of nearer definition come first, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=הַמֶּ֫לֶךְ דָּוִד}}, {{GHGheb|text=הַמֶּ֫לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹה|translate=king David, king Solomon}} (less frequently {{GHGheb|text=דָּוִד הַמֶּ֫לֶךְ}} as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=13|verse=39}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=2|verse=17}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=12|verse=2|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=8|verse=29}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=9|verse=15|hidebook=1}}, and in late Hebrew, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Hag|chapter=1|verse=1}}, 15 [cf. the Aramaic order {{GHGheb|text=דריוש מלבא}}], and often in Chron.).—A chiasmus occurs in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=45|verse=4}}, the name standing after the defining noun in the first part of the verse, and before it in the parallel clause.

{{GHGmargin-letter|131|h}}
2. When the {{GHGterm|nota accusativi}} ({{GHGheb|text=אֵת}}, {{GHGheb|text=אֶת־}}) or a preposition precedes the first substantive, it ''may'' be repeated before the noun in apposition, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=4|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=22|verse=2|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=24|verse=4|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=47|verse=29|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=66|verse=21}}; this usually occurs when the nearer definition precedes a ''proper name''. As a rule, however, the repetition does not take place ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=18|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=33|verse=18}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=2|verse=14}}). A noun in apposition is made determinate, even after a noun with a prefix, in the ordinary way, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=12|verse=13}} {{GHGheb|text=בִּירֽוּשָׁלַ֫יִם הָעִיר|translate=in Jerusalem, the city which}}, &c.<ref>In {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=11|verse=8}} participles after {{GHGheb|text=לְכָל־נָשָׁיו}}, as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=10|verse=6}} after {{GHGheb|text=אֶת־גְּדֹלֵי הָעִיר}}, in 19:2 after a determinate accusative, and in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Hag|chapter=1|verse=4}} after {{GHGheb|text=בְּבָֽתֵּיכֶם}}, are used ''without'' the article; these, however, are probably to be explained not as in apposition, but according to {{GHGpar|118|p}}.</ref>

{{GHGmargin-letter|131|i}}
3. Sometimes a second adjective is used in apposition to a preceding adjective, in order to modify in some way the meaning of the first, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=13|verse=19}} {{GHGheb|text=בַּהֶ֫רֶת לְבָנָה אֲדַמְדָּ֑מֶת|translate=a white-reddish}} (light red) ''bright spot''.

{{GHGmargin-letter|131|k}}
4. ''Permutation'' is to be regarded as a variety of apposition. It is not complementary like apposition proper (see ''a'' above), but rather ''defines'' the preceding substantive (or pronoun, see below), in order to prevent any possible misunderstanding. This includes cases like {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=9|verse=4}} ''with the life thereof'' (which is) ''the blood thereof''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=22|verse=30}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=2|verse=26}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=7|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=3|verse=4}} ''an hundred thousand rams, the wool'', i.e. the wool of the rams; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=25|verse=15}} ''this cup of the wine'', that is ''of fury'' (but {{GHGheb|text=הַֽחֵמָה}} is probably a gloss); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=42|verse=25}} ''he poured upon him fury'', namely ''his anger'';<ref>But {{GHGheb|text=מַ֫יִם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=6|verse=17}} (cf. 7:6) is to be regarded as a later gloss upon the archaic {{GHGheb|text=מַבּוּל}}.</ref> but especially the examples in which such a permutative is added to a preceding pronoun, viz.—

{{GHGmargin-letter|131|l}}
(''a'') To a separate pronoun, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=7|verse=11}}; with regard to the vocative, cf. {{GHGpar|126|f}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|131|m}}
(''b'') To an accusative suffix, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=2|verse=6}} ''she saw him, the child'' (unless {{GHGheb|text=אֶת־הַיּ׳}} be a later gloss); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=35|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=13|verse=57}}<sup> ''b''</sup>, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=19|verse=21}} (where, indeed, {{GHGheb|text=הַבָּשָׂר}} appears to be a late gloss); 21:13, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=16|verse=15}} {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>th.}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=9|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=31|verse=2|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=3|verse=21}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=2|verse=21}} (according to Delitzsch rather a double accusative).<ref>For {{GHGheb|text=וַיְשַׁנּוֹ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=21|verse=14}} either’ {{GHGheb|text=וַיְשַׁנֶּה}} is to be read or the {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>thîbh}} is to be explained according to {{GHGpar|75|b}}, note. Also {{GHGheb|text=יִלְכְּדֻנוֹ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=5|verse=22}} has hardly preserved the correct form.</ref>

{{GHGmargin-letter|131|n}}
(''c'') To a noun-suffix, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=10|verse=3}} {{GHGheb|text=בְּבֹאוֹ הָאִישׁ|translate=when he went in, the man}}; 42:14; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=13|verse=4}} (?), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=3|verse=12}}; so also after a preposition with suffix, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=4|verse=10}} {{GHGheb|text=אִי לוֹ הָֽאֶחָד|translate=woe to him, the one alone}}; with a repetition of the preposition, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=32|verse=33}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=1|verse=2}} {{GHGheb|text=לָהֶם לִבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל|translate=to them, to the children of Israel}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=21|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=51|verse=56}},<section end=par131 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>
